::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 9th 1899  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS  West Sussex County Record Office/ Add. 16,944/1
:::

Dear [Madam](people/person_2234.qmd)
[Macmillan](organizations/other_111.qmd) published both series of the [Store House of Stories](cmy_books/cmybook_83.qmd).  I do not know that the [second series](cmy_books/cmybook_96.qmd) is gone out of print, I should think they had it in stock.  If not I could lend it to you- or my own old copy of ‘[the Puzzle for a curious girl](other_books/otherbook_619.qmd)’  which I inherited from my mother, and is somewhere in the house, though I cannot lay my hand on it without a search.[^1]  It has a red back, and illustrations at the top of the chapters, in the style of 1810-20, I should say - but of course they may have been made for the edition.

But I should hardly think the idea or the writing were Addisonian though it is a very clever story.  It seems to me to be of a later period than Mrs Dorothy Kilner’s [Jemima Placid](other_books/otherbook_742.qmd) and the ‘little gilt books’ of the ‘corner of St Paul’s Church Yard

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: CMY had reprinted S.W., *A Puzzle for a Curious Girl* (London: Tabart and Harris ?1803) in *A Storehouse of Stories* (London: Macmillan 1870).
